keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for 1817-1819 (its Republic of Venezuela ends in 1814). The Third Republic page gives no territory; only Bolívar state (Angostura, the Orinoco) is certain. 'The year 1818 saw a stalemate between the patriots based in Angostura' and the royalists entrenched in Caracas (Venezuelan War of Independence page). No area on any page, so the infobox comparison could not be made.

correction.text: 'elections only took place in the areas of southern Venezuela and Margarita Island controlled by the patriot forces' (Congress of Angostura, 15 February 1819)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Congress page names 'southern Venezuela and Margarita Island' as the patriot-held areas in 1819; Bolívar state and Nueva Esparta are the researcher's reading. Apure and the Llanos (where Páez defeated Morillo in 1819) are not claimed by any page as part of the Republic.

region.text: Guayana and Angostura, taken from the royalists in the Guayana Campaign

ledger.note: 19 July 1817: the Guayana Campaign gives the republicans a base on the Orinoco. Infobox 'Guyana Campaign: 19 July 1817'; 'Piar and Mariño had occupied defenceless Angostura' before Bolívar arrived (Venezuelan War of Independence page). The pages give no boundary.

region.text: Margarita Island, shown in patriot hands at the Congress of Angostura

ledger.note: February 1819: Margarita Island votes at Angostura. 'elections only took place in the areas of southern Venezuela and Margarita Island controlled by the patriot forces'; the Congress 'met from February 15, 1819'. Page silent on when Margarita came under patriot control; 1819 is the first date the island is shown held.

region.text: the patriot-held south of Venezuela and Margarita, joined with New Granada

ledger.note: 17 December 1819: the Congress of Angostura creates the Republic of Colombia. 'On December 17, 1819, the Fundamental Law of the Republic of Colombia' was enacted in Angostura; the Venezuelan constitution of 1819 was 'quickly made obsolete'.
17 December 1819: the Third Republic of Venezuela ends in Gran Colombia. 'The Republic ended after the Congress of Angostura of 1819 decreed the union of Venezuela with New Granada.'

wars.name: Venezuelan War of Independence (1817-1819 phase)

zones.text: Guayana and Angostura, the republicans' base on the Orinoco

wars.outcome: The republicans hold Guayana and the Orinoco from 1817; 'a stalemate' in 1818 between the patriots at Angostura and Morillo's royalists in Caracas; in 1819 the patriots defeat Morillo and Morales in Apure and win Boyacá in August 1819; the Congress of Angostura joins Venezuela and New Granada on 17 December 1819.
wars.note: Page silent on dates for the capture of Angostura (July 1817) and Piar's execution; the Third Republic page's 19 July 1817 is the infobox date of the Guayana Campaign.

certainty.note: No frontier is described on any page: the republic is a patriot base on the Orinoco facing royalist Caracas, with no surveyed or treaty line.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for 1817-1819 (Republic of Venezuela ends in 1814, Venezuela starts in 1834). The captaincy-general-of-venezuela dossier (am-08-a) records the 1817 loss of Angostura and Guayana with counterpart 'republic-of-venezuela', which is the Cliopatria row of 1811-1814: the reviewer should re-point that counterpart to third-republic-of-venezuela.
Thin: no page opened gives the republic's territory beyond 'southern Venezuela and Margarita Island' (1819) or the date of Piar's execution or of the capture of Angostura (the infobox gives 19 July 1817 for the Guayana Campaign only). Angostura is Ciudad Bolívar in the gazetteer. A gap-filler should open the Spanish 'Campaña de Guayana' article.
Gran Colombia is proclaimed at Angostura on 17 December 1819; the gran-colombia dossier starts in December 1819 with predecessors new-granada and spanish-empire, so the Third Republic should be added there as a third predecessor.
